description: A Claude skill that turns vibecoded, AI-looking UI into a designed interface
readme_excerpt:
# unslop

Created by Damir Sokolovsky ([@heydamir](https://x.com/heydamir)), who started the [Unslopping series](https://x.com/heydamir/status/2115063463063998736) on X.

![A vibecoded dashboard unslopping itself, frame by frame](skills/unslop/references/refs/story-dashboard-frames.webp)

unslop is a skill for Claude Code and Codex that turns vibecoded, AI-looking UI into a designed interface with its own character. It finds the slop first, the purple gradients, glows, emoji labels, shouty copy and uneven spacing, then sets a direction from your product and fixes the screen pass by pass like a designer doing a redline review. It works in whatever your screen is built with, like Next.js, React, Vue, Svelte, Tailwind or plain HTML and CSS, on dashboards, apps and landing pages, and even on a live site when all you have is a link.

## Install

For Claude Code, copy the skill into your skills folder.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/heydamir/unslop
mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills && cp -r unslop/skills/unslop ~/.claude/skills/
```

For a single project, copy it into `.claude/skills/` inside that project instead.

For Codex, ask it to install the skill straight from this repo.

```
$skill-installer install https://github.com/heydamir/unslop/tree/main/skills/unslop
```

Or copy it by hand into `~/.agents/skills/`, or into `.agents/skills/` inside a single project.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/heydamir/unslop
mkdir -p ~/.agents/skills && cp -r unslop/skills/unslop ~/.agents/skills/
```

To snapshot a live site or create a story video, install Playwright and its Chromium browser from the project directory where you run the skill:

```bash
npm install -D playwright
npx playwright install chromium
```

Story videos also require ffmpeg installed and available on your PATH.

## Use

In Claude Code, type `/unslop` with what you want. In Codex, type `$unslop` the same way. Or just ask in your own words and the agent picks the skill up by itself.

```
/unslop this dashboard
/unslop the hero of https://example.com
/unslop my landing page and make the story video so I can post it
```

It audits the screen and proposes a direction before it edits anything, so you can steer it early. If the screen is already good, it tells you so and suggests a few small refinements instead of redesigning it.

## What it does

- **Audit.** Lists every sign of slop with where it lives.
- **Direction.** Character, world, the one or two moments that carry the color, and a signature detail, all taken from your product.
- **Passes.** Spacing, color, icons, copy, type, layout, details, visuals and motion, in that order.
- **Visuals.** Shows your product instead of a glossy blob. When a hero needs a scene or an object, it can generate one through an image service like fal, Replicate, OpenAI images or Higgsfield. If none is connected, it offers to connect one as an MCP server, and it shows the prompt and asks before every paid generation. Dashboards and apps rarely need one.
- **Story video.** A square video under 10 seconds of your screen unslopping itself, ready to post. It needs Playwright and ffmpeg.

Try it on the two vibecoded screens in [examples](examples).

## Hire the unslopper

Would rather have a designer do it? Damir unslops one key screen in 3 days, built in your stack, at [heydamir.design/unslop](https://heydamir.design/unslop).

## License

[CC BY 4.0](LICENSE). Use it, change it and share it, including commercially, as long as you credit Damir Sokolovsky ([@heydamir](https://x.com/heydamir)) and link back to this repository.

description: 244 pixel art effects, every one a small piece of code. Plus a Claude Code skill to make your own.
readme_excerpt: # pixelfx. **244 pixel art effects and animations, every one a small piece of code.** Fire, explosions, magic, weather, UI, pickups, critters and more. Play them live, recolor and mirror them, drop them into a browser game, or export sprite sheets for any engine. Plus a Claude Code skill that makes new ones the way a picky pixel artist would: draft, render, look, refine. Every effect that involves a character is **acted out**: he winds up, lets go, freezes on contact and recovers, and a target takes the hit. Twelve whole moves chain the effects into attacks from wind-up to recovery. **[open the gallery](https://patch-gg.github.io/pixelfx/)** · [catalog](docs/CATALOG.md) · [acting](#acting) · [the skill](#the-skill) · [make your own](#make-your-own) · [how it works](#how-it-works) The method is [Hugo Duprez](https://x.com/HugoDuprez)'s, from [How to make (good) pixel art effects with Claude](https://www.spritefusion.com/blog/how-to-make-good-pixel-art-effects-with-claude): code is clay, trust your eyes, feed your references. His [open-source effects](https://www.spritefusion.com/pixel-art-vfx) at Sprite Fusion set the bar, and `src/core/sim.js` and the effects that say so at the top adapt his code. description: One-click character swap for videos: an open-source, local Higgsfield Genjutsu alternative built on ComfyUI and MiniMax H3, with FLUX.3 Klein relighting.
readme_excerpt:
# Openjutsu

An open-source, Genjutsu-style character and object swap for video. Drop a video and a character photo, press **Generate**, and the main person in the video is replaced by your character. Or change their hair or clothes, remove something, or put them somewhere else. The camera, cuts, motion and soundtrack stay. Everything runs on open weights on your own GPU: MiniMax H3 for the video, SAM 3.1 to track people, and Qwen3-VL 8B to describe the pictures and shots.

The app is a small Next.js front end over a ComfyUI workflow. It uses [`@comfyorg/sdk`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@comfyorg/sdk), following Comfy's [comfy-reshoot](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/comfy-reshoot) reference app.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2d8d763a-1764-49a6-9116-d6d1be661ff6

| Advanced: several people, pick who becomes who | Object swap: paint where it goes |
| --- | --- |
| ![Two people swapped, each from their own photo](docs/media/advanced_swap.jpg) | ![Sunglasses painted onto a person's eyes](docs/media/object_swap.jpg) |
| **From picture: a new look and place from one picture** | **Post-processing: fix faces** |
| ![A video frame and a picture combined into a posed picture, then a video](docs/media/from_picture.jpg) | ![A small face redrawn at close-up size](docs/media/fix_faces.jpg) |

**From picture → Relight: new light in the same pass**

![A video frame and a picture combined into a posed picture under golden backlight, then a video that keeps the light, with the seventeen light looks below](docs/media/relight.jpg)

## First visit: visual describer

The welcome page lets you choose the vision-language model that describes pictures and video frames and writes prompts. Qwen3-VL 8B INT8 remains the default; Qwen3-VL 4B FP8 and Gemma 4 E2B INT8 are smaller alternatives. Install a compatible single-file model including its vision weights in `ComfyUI/models/text_encoders`, then press **Refresh models**. Other installed models can be selected if they support image/video input and text generation through ComfyUI's CLIPLoader and Generate Text nodes. Text-only models and files requiring a different loader are unsuitable.

Choose according to available VRAM and leave room for image/video context and working memory; file size is not a VRAM requirement, and H3 generation has separate memory needs. Your selection is saved in this browser and used for swaps, prompt descriptions and **Find people**. Reopen **Welcome & models** to change it, or use **Visual describer** under Model components. Alternative describers may change prompt quality and person matching. **Set up later** opens the editor; generation still checks the required files. The separate H3 text encoder remains unchanged.

## Modes

- **Simple motion transfer**: available. One character replaces the main person (the one who fills the most of the frame). Runs `workflows/simple.api.json`, exported from `H3 One-Click Single Swap (DMAD 6 step).json`.
- **Advanced motion transfer**: available. 1–4 characters, each with an optional role; every tracked person is matched to a role per shot, and people without a character stay untouched. Runs `workflows/advanced.api.json`, exported from `H3 One-Click Advanced Swap (DMAD 6 step).json`; **One pass per person** (two characters) runs `workflows/advanced_maxq.api.json`.
- **Object swap**: available. **Change** what SAM tracks (hair, a jacket, a car) into what you describe or show in a picture; **Remove** it; or change the **Background** around it (`person` stays). Only that area is regenerated. Runs `workflows/object.api.json`, exported from `H3 One-Click Object Swap (DMAD 6 step).json`.
- **From picture** (under Object swap): FLUX prepares the character in the raw video frame's pose and body cut while keeping the character picture's background. Review or regenerate the image, then choose **Use this image** to set the video length, video and motion-reference resolutions, models, LoRAs, steps and seed. SolarRenderer defaults to four

description: Install Linux next to Windows without a USB stick
readme_excerpt:
Install Linux next to Windows without a USB stick.

## What it is hop is a single Windows app that installs Linux alongside Windows. Pick a system, choose a drive, drag to choose how much space it gets, and click Install. There's no USB stick to find and nothing to install first. ## What it does - **Downloads from official sources.** It gets the ISO from the project's own server and verifies its checksum where the project publishes one. You can also use an ISO you already have. - **Makes room safely.** It checks your PC first, and nothing on the disk changes until those checks pass. - **Frees space that's stuck.** A drive can show plenty free and still refuse to shrink, because of files Windows can't move. Make room clears them in one click and puts your settings back afterwards. - **Goes where there's room.** Shrink C: or another drive, use free space, or use a second disk inside the PC. If C: is full, hop suggests a drive that isn't, and the download can go elsewhere too. - **Tells you what to click.** It lists the exact choices to make in the Linux installer. - **Gets you unstuck.** If the PC goes back to Windows, reopening hop explains why and can restart into the BIOS. - **Cleans up after itself.** Undo gives the space back to the drive it came from, and it can also remove another Linux already on the drive. - **Can replace Windows entirely, for the systems where hop has seen it work:** Ubuntu, Xubuntu, Ubuntu Budgie, Ubuntu Cinnamon, Edubuntu, Ubuntu Studio, Zorin OS, Fedora Workstation, Ultramarine, elementary OS, Debian, Arch and Omarchy. It's a separate choice with its own warning, and you have to type ERASE. hop only makes the installer, which copies itself to memory so it can erase the disk it started from when you tell it to. It needs more memory than the ISO's size, and it's only offered for systems where hop has seen it erase a disk and start again afterwards. **Systems:** elementary OS, Ubuntu and its flavours (Budgie, Xubuntu, Lubuntu, Cinnamon, Unity, Edubuntu, Studio), Linux Mint, Pop!_OS, Zorin OS, Debian, Fedora Workstation, Ultramarine, CachyOS, Arch Linux and Omarchy. Other Ubuntu-based ISOs should work too, if you choose the file yourself. Kubuntu isn't supported, because its ISO has a file too big for FAT32. CachyOS, Arch, Omarchy and Pop!_OS need Secure Boot off. Omarchy also needs BitLocker fully off on its disk, not paused, and hop refuses until it is. hop won't turn it off for you. Debian, CachyOS, Linux Mint and Zorin OS can't go on a second disk yet. **Needs:** Windows 10 (1803 or newer) or 11, on a UEFI PC with a GPT disk, which is nearly every PC sold with them. Linux has to go on a disk inside the PC, not a USB drive.

## How it works A USB installer is just a FAT32 drive with the ISO's files on it. hop makes the same thing on your internal disk: ``` Before [ EFI ][ C: Windows ][ Recovery ] After [ EFI ][ C: Windows ][ Installer ][ Linux ][ Recovery ] ``` 1. **Download and check** the ISO, and confirm it's a system hop can install. 2. **Make room** after the drive you chose, using free space first and shrinking the drive only if needed. 3. **Copy** the ISO's files onto a small FAT32 partition, and check each one. 4. **Add a startup entry** with the ISO's signed boot loader, for the next restart only. 5. **Re

# nv-uefi-unlocker

[中文](README.md) | [English](README.en.md)

**你的 GeForce 正以半速跑 AI——这个工具在驱动加载前把它修复。**

[![version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-2.1.8-brightgreen)](https://github.com/physicsdolphin/nv-uefi-unlocker/releases/latest)
[![GeForce](https://img.shields.io/badge/GeForce-GTX%2016%20%7C%20RTX%2020%2F30%2F40-green)](docs/compatibility.md)
[![platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-UEFI%20%E9%A2%84%E9%A9%B1%E5%8A%A8%20%7C%20Win%20%2F%20Linux%20%2F%20Hackintosh-blue)](docs/faq.md)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-GPL--2.0-blue)](LICENSE)
[![stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/physicsdolphin/nv-uefi-unlocker?label=stars&color=yellow)](https://github.com/physicsdolphin/nv-uefi-unlocker/stargazers)

**实测 FP16 / BF16 / TF32 张量吞吐最高约 2.6× · FP8 最高约 1.9× · 图像 / 视频生成 +14–75% · DirectML 推理算子最高 +94% · 无 VBIOS 刷写，断电即复原**（逐卡数据见[兼容性矩阵](docs/compatibility.md)；增益受功耗墙与精度路径制约）

GTX 16 + RTX 20 + RTX 30 + RTX 40 系列通用的 UEFI 预驱动 NVIDIA GPU 解锁工具。

解开 NVIDIA 显卡的 Tensor 计算性能限制。从 U 盘启动，解锁后自动进入 Windows 或 Linux 或任意操作系统，无需刷写 VBIOS；断电后恢复原状。

[观看项目宣传片 ↗](https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1d6xN66ECM/)

## 兼容性速览

| 系列 | 支持情况 |
| --- | --- |
| GTX 16 · Turing | 理论兼容，欢迎实机验证 |
| RTX 20 · Turing | 全系兼容；部分型号有已知问题，见完整矩阵 |
| RTX 30 · Ampere GA10x | 全系兼容，支持笔记本与台式 |
| RTX 40 · Ada | 全系兼容，支持笔记本与台式 |
| Pascal 及更早 / GA100 / RTX 50 | 不支持 |

[完整兼容性矩阵与逐卡实测](docs/compatibility.md) · [常见问题](docs/faq.md)

## 开始使用

### 1. 获取工具并检查前置条件

从 [Releases](https://github.com/physicsdolphin/nv-uefi-unlocker/releases) 下载并解压发布包。发布包不附带 NVIDIA 固件，制盘脚本会自动下载指定版本并校验、生成所需文件。

准备一个 FAT32 U 盘，先备份其中的文件。目标机器须使用 UEFI 启动，关闭 Secure Boot，或为 EFI 自签并信任证书。笔记本优先使用独显直连，从系统选择“重启”后进入一次性启动菜单。

**Turing 用户先在目标 Windows 的管理员 PowerShell 运行一次，再重启：**

```powershell
.\enable-turing-unlock.ps1
```

重启后确认 GSP 固件已运行，再制作 U 盘。Linux Turing 目标同样需要 GSP-RM；详见 [GSP 前置说明](docs/faq.md#turing)。Linux 用户还应检查 [RTD3](docs/faq.md#linux)，避免进入系统后掉电丢失解锁。

### 2. 制作启动 U 盘

在**目标机**（要解锁的机器）的解压目录直接运行：脚本自动识别本机显卡代际，只生成并下载对应固件。

Windows PowerShell：

```powershell
.\make-usbroot.ps1
```

Linux / WSL / Git Bash：

```bash
bash make-usbroot.sh
```

在另一台机器上制作时显式指定代际：40 系 `-Family 40`，30 系 `30`，20 / 16 系 `20`。`-Family all` 把三代固件全部打进同一张 U 盘（一条命令即可服务多种卡）。

Windows 需要 PowerShell 5+；Linux 版需要 glibc ≥ 2.34（如 Ubuntu 22.04+ / Debian 12+）。首次生成需要联网，下载或校验失败时先处理错误，不要换固件版本。

生成的文件位于本地 `usbroot/`。将脚本完成时列出的固件文件复制到 U 盘根目录，再把 `BOOTX64.EFI` 放入 `EFI/BOOT/`。其余抽取中间文件不需要复制。

```text
U 盘（FAT32）
├── EFI/BOOT/BOOTX64.EFI
└── 固件文件（脚本末尾列出的 .bin 文件）
```

保留脚本生成的 `v67-*.bin` 解锁文件。[完整文件清单与用途](docs/faq.md#usb)。

替换已有 `EFI/BOOT/BOOTX64.EFI` 前先备份。不要复制到系统 ESP，也不需要调整永久启动顺序。完整文件用途、异机制盘、多卡选择和其他选项见 [USB 文件与选项](docs/faq.md#usb)。

### 3. 启动并验证

1. 从固件的一次性启动菜单选择 U 盘。
2. 版本屏按 **空格或回车**运行；其他键或 30 秒不操作会中止事务并交回系统引导器。目标 GPU 暂时黑屏或冻结末帧属正常现象。
3. 等待工具完成并自动链回系统，日志在 U 盘根目录 `loader.log`。
4. Windows 下用发布包的 `ssdiag-x86_64-windows.exe` 检查系统内状态，并用相同负载比较解锁前后的性能。Linux 可在源码仓库运行 `sudo python3 tools/diag-unlock.py`。详见 [验证与修复](docs/faq.md#ssdiag)。每次冷启动需要重放。

遇到 STOP、异常或黑屏卡死，**同会话不要重试**；完全断电后拔 U 盘，走原系统引导，再按 [恢复说明](docs/faq.md#recovery)检查。

让 Agent 帮忙部署：[部署指南](AGENTS.deploy.md)。可以直接把下面这句话交给它：

> 请根据 https://github.com/physicsdolphin/nv-uefi-unlocker/blob/main/AGENTS.deploy.md ，帮我安装 nv-uefi-unlocker，为我的显卡解锁。

## 自行构建（可选）

使用发布包可跳过本节。需要 Rust 工具链；Windows 选择 MSVC 版本。在仓库根目录运行：

```text
rustup target add x86_64-unknown-uefi
cargo build --release
cargo efi-tx
```

EFI 程序生成在 `target/x86_64-unknown-uefi/release/loader.efi`。用以下命令制作启动文件（40 系示例；30 系改 `-Family 30`，20 / 16 系改 `-Family 20`）：

```powershell
.\release\make-usbroot.ps1 -Family 40 -AssetsExe .\target\release\assets.exe -BootEfi .\target\x86_64-unknown-uefi\release\loader.efi
```

```bash
bash release/make-usbroot.sh --family 40 \
  --assets ./target/release/assets \
  --boot-efi ./target/x86_64-unknown-uefi/release/loader.efi
```

之后按上面的布局复制到 U 盘。[只读诊断、测试与开发说明](docs/faq.md#layout)。

## 与 nvoc 配合

本工具解除 Tensor 计算性能限制；[nvoc](https://github.com/Skyworks-Neo/nvoc) 在系统内提供功耗、电压和超频控制，两者可以叠加。

# dsh-superagent

> **Research prototype for reference only, not an official DeepSeek product.** This code grew out of our team's day-to-day development work, with much of the engineering done by coding agents. Treat it as research code, not production-ready software. It may still contain bugs, and its coding style and engineering practices may be inconsistent. Review and adapt it before using it in your own environment.
>
> We have adapted it for publication, so it is not identical to our internal version or the implementation described in *Exploring Super-agent Design: Towards a More Autonomous Agent System*. Some designs discussed in the article are directions for future development and are not implemented in this prototype.

dsh-superagent is a proactive coding agent for one GitHub repository, packaged as a bundle for [DeepSeek Harness](https://www.deepseek.com/en/harness/). It listens to GitHub and, optionally, Feishu. When someone allowed asks the agent for work, it opens a work item, works on it in its own agent session and directory, and answers in the original conversation, for example with a pull request. A web panel shows what needs a person.

It is also a way of working with an agent: **take as little human attention as possible, and give as much value as possible.** An agent that can act for a whole team can also waste a whole team's attention, so it acts only when asked or when a rule the team wrote allows it, and speaks only when someone must act or can use a result. [docs/000-philosophy.md](docs/000-philosophy.md) explains the principle and what it asks of the operator.

## Setup

Setup has many steps, so an agent does it with you. Ask your coding agent:

> Read SETUP.md in this repository and set up dsh-superagent with me.

It asks one short question at a time, shows the full plan once, and then installs and configures everything. [SETUP.md](SETUP.md) is what it follows.

## Documentation

Read the numbered documents in order; each builds only on the ones before it.

- [000 Philosophy](docs/000-philosophy.md)
- [001 Domain model](docs/001-domain.md)
- [002 Authorization](docs/002-authorization.md)
- [003 Execution](docs/003-execution.md)
- [004 Prompts](docs/004-prompts.md)
- [005 Panel](docs/005-panel.md)
- [006 Deployment](docs/006-deployment.md): manual setup, configuration, upgrades and troubleshooting
- [007 Architecture](docs/007-architecture.md)
- [008 Cookbook](docs/008-cookbook.md): adding a Source

## Development

`pnpm check` runs the typecheck, the tests and the build.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE)

## Why Floorplan? You built an app, probably with a lot of help from AI, and it works. But ask "what happens when someone checks out?" or "what breaks if I change this?" and the honest answer is *no idea*. Floorplan gives you the diagram nobody drew. Ask Claude Code or Codex for a floorplan and a few minutes later you have a map you can explore, ask questions on, and keep up to date as you work. - **For builders:** understand the app you made, in your own words, without reading the code. - **For teams:** onboard someone in minutes, from the big picture down to the exact file. - **For working with AI:** after every change Claude or Codex makes, see exactly which parts it touched and why. ## Floorplan, Archify or Understand Anything? All three turn code into something you can see, and all three are worth knowing.
